item.title: Merck/Kelun Sac-TMT ADC
item.description:
• Summary: Merck (MSD) and partner Kelun announced results from a Phase 3 trial in first-line lung cancer showing that their investigational antibody-drug conjugate Sac-TMT in combination with pembrolizumab (Keytruda) reduced the risk of progression by 65% compared to pembrolizumab alone. The data, presented from a Chinese study, suggest a potential new standard-of-care for first-line non-small cell lung cancer. Sac-TMT is a Trop-2-directed ADC, while pembrolizumab is a PD-1 inhibitor. The combination's superior efficacy marks a significant advance in ADC‑immunotherapy combinations.
  • MoAs: Sac-TMT: Antibody-drug conjugate targeting Trop-2, delivering a cytotoxic payload to cancer cells. Pembrolizumab: PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibitor that reactivates anti-tumor T cells.
  • Sources: Fierce Pharma, STAT News, Endpoints News

item.title: VEGF Bispecifics
item.description:
• Summary: New clinical data have been released for vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) bispecific antibodies being developed by BioNTech, Bristol Myers Squibb, Pfizer, and 3SBio. These bispecifics are designed to simultaneously block multiple angiogenic pathways, potentially offering improved efficacy over standard VEGF inhibitors in various solid tumors.
  • MoAs: VEGF bispecific antibodies inhibit VEGF-A along with a second target (e.g., VEGF-C or another receptor) to block tumor angiogenesis and reduce vascular permeability.
  • Sources: Endpoints News
